Subject: Contract redline: telemetry export & subprocessor limits

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team liked the latency profile. Legal asked me to follow up with two non-negotiable asks before we can move to signature:

1) Remove any right for Redwood to export raw telemetry or model outputs for analytics or training. HealthSync requires that any telemetry leaving our environment be aggregated and under our control.
2) Limit subprocessors to the enumerated list in the DPA; any new subprocessor requires 30-day notice and written approval.

I've attached a redline (HealthSync_redline_v1.pdf) with suggested language. Please confirm whether Product and Security can agree to these changes or suggest concrete mitigations. We are trying to avoid a long procurement loop.

Anna — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Security/Legal (Olga) and Product (Irene) to surface impact and alternative language.

Quick read notes from me:
- Removing export entirely will block our ability to ship aggregate model health dashboards and automated drift alerts.
- We can propose two mitigation paths:
  A) Allow only aggregated, non-reconstructable metrics (no raw outputs or per-session logs) with a 30-day TTL and customer-controlled truncation key.
  B) Allow export through a customer-controlled SFTP/KMS flow where HealthSync owns the keys and ops pulls exports on-demand.

Olga/Irene — can you weigh in on legal/compliance viability and dev effort? If neither path is acceptable we should propose a short mutual action plan so HealthSync understands tradeoffs and timeline.

Next steps I propose: legal propose alternate clause, product surface technical constraints + estimate, and sales (me) confirm whether a short term PO addendum or credit would help.

Thanks Anna / Lauren — I reviewed the redline. HealthSync's asks are reasonable from a privacy posture but we can’t accept a blanket ban on exports without operational and monitoring tradeoffs. Suggested language (high level):

"Redwood will not export raw request/response payloads or de-anonymized model outputs for analytics or training. Redwood may transmit aggregated, non-reconstructable metrics (e.g., per-minute token counts, latency percentiles, error rates) that do not permit reconstruction of customer inputs or outputs. Any telemetry exports to third parties shall be subject to Customer-approved KMS/HSM keying and audit logs. New subprocessors will be added only after Customer is notified and given 30 days to object in writing; Redwood will not engage new subprocessors for processing Customer data during such objection period."

Two notes: 1) we should define "non-reconstructable" in the DPA schedule (I can draft) and 2) we need Security to confirm the KMS & audit log control path is available for Dedicated/Private vs Hosted.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security

Subject: Re: Contract redline: telemetry export & subprocessor limits

Appending Product assessment — thanks for the clear ask. High-level technical implications and mitigations:

1) Telemetry types: we collect (a) raw request/response payloads, (b) token-level logs used for replay/debug, (c) aggregate performance metrics (latency, token rates, error classes), and (d) usage metadata (route, model version). HealthSync's ask forbids (a) and (b).

2) Mitigations we can deliver without a fundamental runtime rewrite:
   - Aggregation with differential TTL: create per-customer aggregated metrics pipeline (latency p50/p95, tokens/min, errors) with a 30-day TTL and hash-salted keys to prevent session reconstruction. We can expose these via the Console and push exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket (customer-managed keys).
   - Query-classification redaction: run an upstream classifier to remove or mask PII/PHI prior to any logs; for HealthSync we can enable stricter redaction thresholds. This is ~2-3 weeks of Product + infra work to validate and +1 week of perf testing.
   - On-demand export: implement a pull-only export where HealthSync triggers an export job; exports contain only aggregated rows and require HSM-backed encryption. This is ~4-6 weeks to build and validate across Hosted/Dedicated.

3) Subprocessors: our infra uses two analytics partners for cost telemetry and one observability vendor. For Dedicated/Private customers we already support an allowlist mode where we do not engage external analytics partners. For Hosted, we can route HealthSync to a Dedicated pool or offer allowlist + audit logs.

Estimated immediate effort to reach a contractual position:
- Draft and review clause (Legal): 2 business days.
- Implement aggregation & TTL + S3 push (Product/Infra): 2-3 weeks (MVP).
- QA/security review for export path & HSM keys: 1 week.

I will attach a telemetry mapping spreadsheet with the pipeline fields we propose to expose so Legal can confirm "non-reconstructable" semantics.

Irene Choi
Director of Product, Runtime
